content: When editing an article, there is a small field labeled Summary located beneath the main edit box. It is strongly recommended to fill in this edit summary field. Doing so facilitates understanding of the changes made to the page for both you and other contributors. Additionally, it is helpful in identifying when specific changes were made to the page. Places Where the Edit Summary Appears The edit summary is displayed in black italics in the following locations: Page history: This shows a list of changes made to the page you edited. User contributions: This lists all the edits you have made. Watchlist: For logged-in users, this lists recent changes to pages you are watching. Diff page: This shows the differences between two edits. Recent changes: This lists all recent edits across the platform. Related changes: This lists recent changes to pages linked to the page you edited. These features, along with the page histories of the articles, are typically used to track all recent changes, including the associated edit summaries. Searching The search function does not index or search edit summaries. They are also not indexed by external search engines. File Upload Summary When uploading an image, you can provide an upload summary. This serves several purposes: It acts as the second part of the automatically generated edit summary in the upload log (the first part includes the file name). It appears as text in the image's history entry. If the image file name is new, it serves as the edit summary for the creation of the image page. The upload summary can also include wikitext for the editable part of the image page, allowing you to: Briefly describe the image. Provide internal or external links. Call templates. Specify one or more categories the image belongs to. The upload summary has a capacity of 250 characters. However, in the upload log, the last part may be truncated because the log can only contain 255 characters, including the uploaded 'filename' text. Note that there is no preview function to check the code for links, template calls, or category tags. However, you can edit the image page after uploading to correct errors or extend the text. Section Title as Automatic Edit Summary When using the section editing feature, the section title is automatically inserted as the initial version or first part of the edit summary. You can add more details after this text. If you provide a long summary, you can delete the section title to stay within the 200-character limit. Post a Comment Feature When starting a new thread on a Talk page, you can optionally use the Post a comment feature (accessible via the + tab next to the edit tab). In this case, the edit summary is automatically set to match the new section header. Rendering of Wikitext and URLs Text in edit summaries renders internal links, including piped links, even when enclosed within brackets. Therefore, copying wikitext into the edit summary box may be preferable to copying text from the preview, except when you want to save space. Other wikitext coding is not interpreted. URLs are rendered as they normally appear, with the URL displayed in parentheses. This provides the same information as in the wikitext but in a different format, along with a possible sequential number.
